svg.title: TOPAK B1 — The authority chain: one axiom, two verified floors, and every effect traced back up
svg.desc: Authority flows down from a single assumed sentence, anchor intent, through anchor issuance bounded by the rules floor, issued rules, the promotion quorum, the policy floor and its bundles, the operators who put successor leases on the log, the lease, and the admit, to an effect. The audit chain runs the same links back up, and no link is assumed except the last. This is how the authority regress ends: one axiom, bounded by two verified floors. Since Batch 34 the operator is a principal and break-glass an emergency seating, both provisional.
svg.text: TOPAK · B1

text.tspan: The authority chain: one axiom, two verified floors, and every effect traced back up

svg.text: Authority flows down from a single assumed sentence, anchor intent, through anchor issuance bounded by the rules floor, issued rules, the promotion quorum, the policy floor and its bundles, the operators who put successor leases on the log, the lease, and the admit, to an effect. The audit chain runs the same links back up, and no link is assumed except the last. This is how the authority regress ends: one
axiom, bounded by two verified floors. Since Batch 34 the operator is a principal and break-glass an emergency seating, both provisional.

text.tspan: Accepted · bootstrap set: no marker possible

svg.text: An authentic issuance at the current anchor epoch is what the anchor intended.
Assumed, not modeled. No safety theorem covers it: a coalition at the capture threshold can issue any rules-floor-conformant roster. That is the headline residual (ToO §7.2).
The trust anchor is the sole issuer of rules. Issue is constrained only by an opaque Authentic, epoch increment and the rules floor; safety must hold for every issuance the anchor could make, so its
composition never enters the proof.
Consensus-ordered; non-erasable as forensic class F4, genesis included (ADR-0028). Authority changes are exactly {promotion, anchor issuance} (ADR-0015).

text.tspan: 2 · The rules floor bounds every issuance (ADR-0026)

svg.text: Part of the verified object: the mechanism rejects any issuance that violates it. Two keys, both directions: a rules-floor change needs an anchor issuance and a promotion under the rules being
replaced.

text.tspan: 3 · Issued rules: the authority-defining set (ADR-0025 §1, with A1 to A3)

svg.text: (a) the promotion roster and its parameters, quorum and minGrant; (b) the break-glass and erasure rosters; (c) the anchor's own key set; (d) any relaxation of the policy floor or new floor exception; (e)
any change to the rules floor, either direction.
(f) the keys the mechanism accepts a signature from in place of its own check: the rung-3 verifier's appraisal key and the bundle-signing key (A1, Batch 17), and since A3 an identity provider's key,

under which an operator's sign-on is accepted (provisional). Replacing any adds authority, so it is an issuance. The first two exist at the reference (ADR-0033 A6); the verifier key is read at every rung-3
grant, renewal and Contested entry (A7, Batch 29), and the only keys in it are test keys, in SIMULATED runs.

(g) the independence criterion in force (B29); (h) the two lists a bundle's load checks read (A2): the entries that may release a reserved label, and the channel targets inside the deployment. (a) is read to
include the operator seats and, at genesis, the first operators' seatings (A3). The rules floor bounds none of the three new things (G10 §2.1).
Genesis rules are resident (ADR-0027): they ship with the mechanism release, are fetched from nowhere, and are epoch 0, the root of the rules-epoch chain. Anchor unavailability blocks change, never
operation. At bootstrap genesis issues no erasure roster.
Everything crossing Build → Run is promoted: bundles, mechanism releases (floor changes included), Personas.
Every counted grant seat must grant (quorum = "all"); a grant-seat deny or abstention denies; a timeout is never a grant. Veto seats (every cell Observer and correlator) can only deny; their
silence is not a veto.
Votes bind to (artifact digest, gate-evidence digest, rules epoch): any rules-epoch change voids in-flight votes. The author is recused by the Vote envelope. Gates enable voting; they do not vote.
A round stalls unless an independent veto seat was leased and the author's cell Observer covered the seal (A2.2, A2.3; A2.2 not yet in the reference, item 46).

A promotion seats (A3, provisional): a promoted seating names a principal, its seat, Persona, bundle revision, confinement and alphabet, and the labels its task may carry; the completed tally grants the
first lease at a fresh fence, with no request from anyone. Not built at the reference (G10 item 88).

The policy floor is in the verified object, Cedar linked into the mechanism and resident. The floor in force is the proposed floor's emergency stage (28 policies, 15c941b9a56a09f7), built in gated stages

from the genesis draft: genesis-provisional, gated, pinned and enforced, ratified only when the bootstrap reviewer finds it fit (ADR-0030 A3; G10 §2.2). It decides operators' requests too, by C1 to C9.
Tightening it is an ordinary promotion; relaxing it adds an anchor issuance; the route is computed (§5).

The bundle is a promoted parameter that can only subtract, at every age; it loads only under a signature from a key in the issued rules (ADR-0044; built at the reference under a dev key, custody (1, 0)).

text.tspan: 6 · Who puts a lease on the log (ADR-0031 A3; ADR-0050 §2, §4)
Accepted · provisional · ADR-0050 · C1, C3, C4

svg.text: A first lease comes from a quorum, granted by the mechanism with no request: an anchor issuance for the rostered seats and the first operators at genesis, a promotion's tally on a seating for everyone
else.
An operator renews what a quorum granted. An operator is a principal on a seat of kind operator, a person, Mediated, treated as havoc. Its requests are signed with its Persona's key and decided by
the floor's nine control entries, C1 to C9, then re-checked by every replica at apply.
Regrant (a successor grant: the next round,
nothing wider), Renew, AttestGates
Add
A live lease and a live peer in the domain; never oneself (C1–C3, C5, C6, C8)
EndRound, Revoke
Deny
A Persona in force, and a live lease or a fresh sign-on; own domain only (C4, C9)
Deny
A Persona in force and a live lease (C4, C7)

text.tspan: 7 · The lease: one composite credential per round (ADR-0031)

svg.text: Twelve fields, a closed schema: principal, seat, persona, epoch, fence, rulesEpoch, bundle, confinement, alphabet, round, role, ttl. A capability that is not a field is not carried.
The fence is the Paxos log index at grant; rulesEpoch and bundle bind the lease to the rules and the bundle revision in force; ttl ≤ T_persona (A2). Renewal only narrows; at most one live lease
per principal.

text.tspan: 8 · The admit: decided, ordered, re-checked (ADR-0015; ADR-0033 §4)

svg.text: Epoch fence → lease → syntactic lift → floor → bundle → consensus-ordered admit. The mechanism checks run twice: before the floor, and again at the entry's log position; an admit that fails the
second is void: ordered, recorded, without effect.
Every effect therefore has a consensus-ordered, signed, authorizing predecessor in the Paxos log. Denials are not ordered, and they are recorded (ADR-0020).

text.tspan: 9 · The effect: exactly {tool invocation, principal emission} (ADR-0015)

svg.text: Build: Invoke, and the emissions Emit, Submit, Vote; Run: Actuate and Report (Consult is ingress, no effect). The effect runs only after commit; a crash between commit and effect leaves no effect,
which is safe.

text.tspan: Custody is a declaration, not a proof

svg.text: Custody instantiates Authentic outside the model, so degrading it reopens nothing; the quorum's archetype
values live inside the rules floor, so degrading them is a mechanism release (ToO §7.7).
At archetype custody loss freezes the rules: the system runs and subtracts but cannot change; the only exit is
re-genesis, a successor system. At archetype custody the key-holders sit at the gate (§7.5).
A solo bootstrap is not a bootstrap: the archetype needs five humans, three key-holders plus two counted grant
seats, disjoint by R5 (ToO §9).

text.tspan: Break-glass is an emergency seating, not a third kind (ADR-0052)
Accepted · provisional · ADR-0052 · C1, C3, C4

svg.text: The roster's quorum activates a seating prepared by promotion: one lease, for one named person and one
round, with the round's task. No successor, no renewal; another round is another quorum. It ends with its round,
which is why R8 was withdrawn (ADR-0013 A1; ADR-0026 W1).
The envelope is an ordinary allowlist, by default every Run entry in force in the domain, so the floor needs no
exception: X1-break-glass is retired, and the floor's one exception is erasure (R6). Erasure stays an admit
against its exception entry (ADR-0015 R2).
The seat is a person's, kind emergency, alphabet Consult, Actuate, Report: R7 has nothing to refuse. Privileged
grants still share one model, a quorum on an anchor-issued roster, bounded by the rules floor.
Not built: a seating prepared by promotion; the reference makes it by the BOOTSTRAP socket (item 92). X1's
retirement stands on a record subject to redesign.

text.tspan: BOOTSTRAP: whoever reaches the socket can seat
Not built · a first lease from a quorum

svg.text: The reference keeps its unsigned operator socket as a marked BOOTSTRAP path that seats and does nothing
else (ADR-0050 §10, R9; ADR-0033 A11). It stands in for the quorum a first lease should come from: D-0050-1 for
that one step, and the debt ADR-0050's provisional status carries.
Everything after the first seating is a signed request decided by C1 to C9: successor grants, renewals, gate
attestations, ends of round, revocations, the fence (ToO §15).
Exit from provisional (item 88): a first lease from a completed tally, the first operators seated by an issuance, a
Regrant at rung 1 or above, an operator's Persona record and lineage, and a review.
E-stop, lease expiry, targeted revocation, epoch fence, abstention, end of round and deny=all need no quorum
and are attributed (ADR-0024 §9, ADR-0031).
Who denies (ADR-0031 A3): both revocation tools are an operator's signed act, with no quorum and no peer; a
revocation or end of round needs a live lease or a fresh sign-on, the fence a live lease. A deny needs no lease,
and the signature is the attribution F2 asks for (ADR-0028).
Ordering is not authorization: where they change replicated state they are still consensus-ordered, or replicas
disagree about what is live (ADR-0033 §4).
Denials are local and unordered: a denied effect never crosses the boundary.
effect: the tool invocation or emission
→ admit: the consensus-ordered decision, kept as F1
→ lease: a quorum's first lease, or a signed operator request under it
→ floor ∧ bundle, at the lease's bundle revision, with the digest of the frozen input
→ rules epoch: the rules in force at grant
→ issuance: the Issue that defined those rules, kept as F4
→ ADR-0025's intent axiom

text.tspan: No link is assumed except the last

svg.text: Every authorization is traceable to a consensus-ordered issuance that defined
the rules in force (ADR-0015).
Votes in the chain are the admit decisions in the consensus log (F3), not the
topic emissions that carry them; commentary is erasable, the vote is not (ToO
Since 2026.10.01 the gate evidence a vote binds to carries a checked proof for
every solver-backed routing holds (ADR-0030 A1). The evidence itself is an
operator's AttestGates: attributed, and still an assertion (ADR-0024 A3;
G10 item 57).
A stop is signed: the signature is the attribution ADR-0028's F2 asks for
(ADR-0031 A3). An activation of an emergency seating is a forensic-floor
record, F5 (ADR-0052 §5).
A declared axiom set
A verified artifact, the policy floor, rather than an axiom set

text.tspan: One axiom (anchor intent), bounded by two verified floors

svg.text: The authority regress now ends the way the policy regress does: a verified floor, with a single sentence assumed above it (§7.6). The two floors are the rules floor (step 2) and the policy floor (step 5).

Not yet in force anywhere: only two of the five bootstrap modules are drafted (BreakGlass_A1 succeeds the second); bootstrap needs a drafted specification and an independent review of the whole corpus (ADR-0029 A2),
and no bootstrap reviewer is engaged (G10 §4). Until then everything ratified is the genesis custodian's declaration, custody (1, 0), and two records are provisional (ToO §9).
